> Hi Morgan,
> Sorry to hear you're having trouble. I looked into how to remove dependencies on rgdal earlier in the year and got rid of most of them but microclima still depends on rgdal and so too do the parts of micro_era5 and micro_ncep that depend on microclima. I have it working on a PC and on linux at my end. I'm a bit swamped with teaching right now but will try and delve into it again in a couple of weeks.
> All the best,
> Mike
>
> On Wednesday, February 28, 2024 at 3:48:31 AM UTC+11 jfle...@vols.utk.edu wrote:
> > Hello,
> >
> > After updating R recently I ran into issues reinstalling mcera5,NicheMapR, and microclima given the retirement of rgdal. Even reverting back to older versions of R, I still could not install any of the packages. Finally, after coming across suggestions to install an archived version of rgdal, I successfully installed all three packages. While it seems like functions in the mcera5 package are working smoothly now, functions in NicheMapR are not. Specifically, the micro_era5() function stops running almost immediately producing the following error:
> >
> >    micro <- micro_era5(loc = loc, dstart = dstart, dfinish = dfinish,
> >                      dem.res = 100,
> >                      Usrhyt = 0.03,
> >                      spatial = file_path)
> >
> > downloading DEM via package elevatr
> > Error in st_transform.sfc(st_geometry(x), crs, ...) :
> >   cannot transform sfc object with missing crs
> > In addition: Warning message:
> > In CPL_crs_from_input(x) :
> >   GDAL Error 1: PROJ: proj_create_from_database: Cannot find proj.db
> >
> >
> > After troubleshooting in the source code, the error arises when the function tries to pull the digital elevation model using microclima::get_dem(). I came across this old post relating a similar issue to the order in which sf (another microclima dependency) and rgdal packages are loaded (https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-sig-geo/2020-September/028412.html). I tried uninstalling and reinstalling sf after rgdal (and adjusting the order in which I load the libraries accordingly) to see if that was also the case here, but I get the same error. I've reported the issue on the microclima github, but I am curious if other NMR users are having similar issues and have suggested work arounds. Perhaps there is another package/function that works for gathering DEMs like microclima::get_dem that doesn't rely on rgdal? Any information and suggestions are greatly appreciated. I have been going a bit crazy trying to find a solution.
> >
> >
> > Operating System: MacOS 13.0
> > R Version: I have tried the latest version 4.3.2 and 4.2.3
> >
> >
> > Best,
> > Morgan Fleming

messages.body_plain:
Dear all,
I'm trying to calculate microclimate data for a particular area by using microclimate().

It's a big data, so I used two computers (both Win10 64-bit) to do the calculations for me and used the same input data with the same code (only the file paths were changed).

Unfortunately, however, one of the computers had an error without sending any error reports or warnings which the results were ridiculously out of whack. For example the calculated soil surface temperature can reach 1.28784026045517e-311.
Strangely, the results from the other computer were all fine.

After comparing the codes, I determined that the input data were exactly the same, but every time after microclimate (micro), there was a problem with its results.
Moreover, after using .Fortran() from the microclimate source code, I get errors as a result.

What I want to ask is, 1) What is the reason for this error? 2) How should I solve this problem?

Thank you,
Linxuan Ma

Linxuan Ma

messages.body_plain:
G'day all,

I think I've figured out the problem here, at least on my system. Hopefully this workaround solves the issue for anybody working in Win10 or later, with nco v4.9.5

The issue is that the system call:

system(cmd) # run ncpdq

only works if the netcdf files to be re-ordered can be found in the nco folder. If you try to call ncpdq on netcdf files stored anywhere else, it isn't recognised as a system command and it will not reorder the dimensions and write the file approrpiately.

Once I moved all the native NCEP files to my NCO folder (C:/nco), and set this to my working directory:

YOUR_LOCATION <- "C:/nco"
dir2do <- YOUR_LOCATIO
setwd(dir2do)

Then the re-oredering worked flawlessly, as per Mike's original script.

These re-ordered NCEP files can then be used locally for micro_ncep().

If anybody knows how to make the system(cmd) call work across the entire system, that would go a long way to avoiding all this in future. In the absence of that, anybody with this issue should be able to work around it by working in the NCO installation directory

Hope that helps

Cheers

Sean

Dear Romain,
It's the maximum energy the stomach can hold per unit of structural volume of the whole organism at a given moment, and its value will therefore depend on your parameter estimates for your species and the energy and water content you give the food. The simplest thing is to play around with the value for E_sm and find one that approximates reality when you look at the model outputs. You could alternatively formally include it in your DEB parameter estimation procedure.
All the best,
Mike

Dear Mike,

we are trying to simulate our lizard's DEB in NichmapR. The outputs are
quite reasonable under some conditions, but more surprising in others:
structural mass decreases during some period of the year (see the figure
 attached). It happens in summer, when temperatures are hot and leaves
very little activity time to the lizard, with the result that the
lizard has very little to eat. I therefore suspect that this creates
conditions in which the flux of mobilized energy that goes to growth +
maintenance (kappa*pc) becomes smaller than maintenance requirements
(pM). When I checked your latest posts on internet, it looks like
NichemapR should be able to control how allocation changes in these
conditions through the parameter starve_mode of the ectotherm function,
which by default should be set to 1, although our output looks like it
is set to 0. In any circumstance, in the version I'm using, which I
believe to be the latest version available (v.3.2.1, from 10/12/2022, or
 maybe I'm missing something?), it seems like this starve_mode thing
hasn't been implemented yet.

So is there any way to control starvation mode in v.3.2.1? or is there a
 newer version around or one that you would be willing to share before
release? Or, do I need to be patient and wait for the next update? Or
maybe, it might just be that I'm doing something wrong?

Thanks in advance,

Romain Richard

Dear Romain,

The 'starvemode' option is something I've recently added.  By default it (starvemode = 1) it uses the reproduction buffer in preference to structure. If you set it to 0 it will go straight to using structure. If you set it to 2 it will use reproduction buffer before it uses reserves.  You can try it out if you get the latest version on github (devtools::install_github('mrke/NicheMapR' - but you need gfortran compilers installed). I'll be writing up that modification as part of a paper I'm putting together on modelling snakes with DEB theory (with other changes to allow feeding in meals as well as laying eggs at maturity stages > 0).

All the best,
Mike

ecto <- ectotherm(nyears = nyears,

                  soilmoist = micro$soilmoist,

                  shadhumid = micro$shadhumid,
                  soilpot = micro$soilpot,
                  shadpot = micro$shadpot,
                  #tcond = micro$tcond,
                  #shadtcond = micro$shadtcond,
                  rainfall = RAINFALL,
                  #rainhr = rep(-1,nrow(micro$metout)),
                  #preshr = rep(101325 * ((1 - (0.0065 * as.numeric(ALTT) / 288)) ^ (1/0.190284)), nrow(metout)),
                  elev = as.numeric(ALTT),
                  longitude = longlat[1],
                  latitude = longlat[2])

The ectotherm model when run with default inputs expects the output of one of the 'micro_xxx' functions (e.g. 'micro_global') that has the name 'micro'. Those 'micro_xxx' function are wrappers that set the microclimate model inputs up for different data sets, e.g. the NCEP or ERA5 or terraclimate data sets (micro_ncep, micro_era5, micro_terra). The way you ran the microclimate model, from that example, was more 'under the hood' where you specify all the inputs explicitly and you can include your own local weather data. But it was missing the step where the final list of outputs is put together in the way the ectotherm model wants them.

Hope that all makes sense. I set it up this way to make it easy to run the ectotherm model after running one of the 'micro_' functions, but if you set it up more manually you need to add a bit more code to properly feed in the input data.

All the best,
Mike
